exposure: enrollment in RIPPLE program (funded intravenous iron supplementation)
cohort: The study included 1206 pregnant patients from a single centre, categorized into low-income, non-low-income, and RIPPLE program participants (low-income receiving funded intravenous iron).
finding: Anemia at delivery was significantly more frequent in RIPPLE participants (54%), who exhibited lower nadir hemoglobin and ferritin, compared to low-income (10%) and non-low-income (7%) groups, indicating that disparities in care persisted despite funding for iron supplementation.
